The true impact is lower than our estimate, so the answer is B.

Purchase means by group:

| push_assigned | push_delivered | Mean purchases | Customers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 69.3 | 5,057 |
| 1 | 0 | 51.9 | 1,396 |
| 1 | 1 | 79.4 | 3,547 |

The regression gives a coefficient of +27.6 on `push_delivered`, which would be the estimated effect of receiving the push.

That figure is biased upward. Customers whose push was not delivered, probably those with older phones, buy much less (51.9) than the typical control customer (69.3). The regression therefore compares delivered customers against a weak baseline.

Delivery is randomised through assignment, so a fairer comparison uses only customers who could receive the push:
- About 28% of the assigned group did not receive it.
- Control customers who would have received it had they been assigned buy about (69.3 − 0.28 × 51.9) / 0.72 ≈ 76.2 on average.
- The delivered group buys 79.4 on average, so the effect on those who actually receive the push is about 79.4 − 76.2 ≈ 3.2.

That is far below the regression estimate of 27.6.

ANSWER: B
